input.quote: 9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and incident-based termination (9.1–9.3), and 8.1 fixes a three-year term with twelve-month Order Form renewals. No convenience termination right exists for Customer anywhere in the Agreement (27.3 is force-majeure specific and 6.2/19.4 are remedy-based), which is a deviation for a term longer than 12 months. Vendor likewise has no convenience right today, but that is not stated expressly. We inserted a new 9.4 giving Customer a 30 days' notice convenience exit and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term; the pro-rata refund element is already met by Section 10.2, which requires Vendor to refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, so we did not restate it.

proposal.summary: Add Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice and bar Vendor convenience termination during a committed term
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The three-year term gives us no way out without cause, so we added a Customer convenience exit on thirty days' notice and confirmed Vendor has no matching right during a committed term; prepaid Fees are already refunded under Section 10.2.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
mappings.quote: Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination

mappings.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
